title: Cost attribution waterfall + latency distribution overlay for model-route telemetry
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Design and spec a combined visualization for per-model & per-route pages that surfaces both fine-grained cost attribution and latency distributions in a single, compact canvas. The goal is to help engineers and SREs quickly identify whether latency outliers or token-cost composition are driving user-facing spend and SLA issues. This ticket covers the UX, interaction patterns, chart-level specs, and handoff artifacts for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A compact canvas mock (Figma) that combines: a stacked cost-attribution waterfall and an overlaid latency distribution (violin) aligned to the same route/model time window
Hover and click interactions defined: tooltip content, drilldown to microtrace link, and switch-to-compare-model-mode
Design tokens and color palette documented and accessible to frontend: color hexes for cost components, latency overlay, and thresholds
Accessibility notes included: screen-reader-friendly table alternative, color contrast ratios, and keyboard interactions for drilldown
Developer handoff packet with sample mock CSVs and API field mapping in Confluence
decisions: Use violin plots for latency distribution rather than boxplots to surface multimodal latency patterns we observe in production (cold-KV, cached, batched) .
Overlay violin on the primary x-axis (time-of-snapshot) and align vertical centerline with waterfall midline so tooltips can reference both charts simultaneously.

Stacked waterfall order: credits/refunds (top), cache savings (negative), prompt tokens, system tokens, response tokens, batching overhead, model multiplier cost. This order maximizes readability of net cost per request.
Default aggregation window: 5m for route-level view, 1m for model variant zoom. Allow user control down to 30s for high-traffic routes.
Use color-blind-safe palette; differentiate cost components by hue and latency overlay by a semitransparent pattern (diagonal hatch available as a fallback for mono print).
Show absolute and normalized cost toggles (USD per 1k requests vs USD per token) in toolbar; persistent preference stored in user settings.
Do not attempt predictive smoothing on violin distributions by default; expose optional smoothing toggle for trend-focused users.
tradeoffs: Violin plots show fine distribution detail but can be visually dense for low-volume routes; fallback to boxplot at sample_count < 50 to avoid misleading shapes.
Overlaying two dense charts increases cognitive load on first glance; mitigated via progressive disclosure (collapsed waterfall summary vs expanded view) and clear microcopy.

Computing violin distributions at very high cardinality (many model variants) is expensive server-side; we will precompute histograms for 1m/5m buckets in the metrics pipeline and limit live compuation to small windows.
Showing both cost and latency on the same canvas prevents tab-switching but constrains vertical space; the design uses a tight split with a responsive collapse for narrow viewports.
chart_specs: Waterfall: stacked bars per aggregation interval (default 5m). X-axis = time window center. Y-axis (cost) = USD. Bar segments: credits/refunds (positive), cache_savings (negative, shown below axis), prompt_tokens, system_tokens, response_tokens, batching_overhead, model_multiplier. Show numeric labels on hover and p50/p95 annotations at top of bar.

Latency overlay: violin plot per aggregation interval, drawn behind the waterfall but semitransparent (opacity 0.22). Violin width scales with sample_count to avoid noise. Violin vertical span represents latency density; overlay includes median line and dashed p95 marker.

Tooltip: unified tooltip when hovering a time interval. Fields: time window, request_count, sample_count, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_total_usd, breakdown by segment (with absolute and per-request values), cache_hit_rate, avg_tokens_prompt/response, model_variant. Include link buttons: 'Open microtrace' (links to trace view), 'Open route logs'
interactions: Hover: unified tooltip for the time bin. Highlight corresponding segments in both waterfall and violin. Keyboard focus mimics hover.
Click on a bar/violin region: expand a right-side panel with microtrace list and example requests (sampled), with actionable items: create support ticket, open PR, compare model variants.

Compare-mode toggle: select up to 2 model variants to display difference waterfall (positive/negative) and overlay difference violin in a contrasting color. Support 'pin as baseline' to lock one variant.
Collapse/expand: Default collapsed waterfall shows net cost + small sparkline; expand reveals full stacked segments and violin. Persists per-user and per-route.
Export: CSV/PNG export available for the current view. CSV includes histogram buckets for latency and exact segment costs per interval.
accessibility_notes: All information accessible via an alternative data table view with same columns as tooltips. Table available via 'View data' button and keyboard shortcut.
Color choices meet WCAG AA for normal text contrast where used for labels. Use additional patterns/hatches to encode critical thresholds for color-blind users.
Interactive elements reachable and operable via keyboard. Tooltips exposed to screen readers with aria-live announcements for dynamic updates.
Provide textual summary for low-vision users that states: 'In the last 24h, X% of cost driven by response tokens; median latency Y ms; p95 Z ms; cache hit rate H%.'
